For this season, the system format remained the same as the [[2016–17 Honduran Liga Nacional|previous season]]. The tournament started on 28 July 2017 and ended on 19 May 2018. The season was divided into two halves (Apertura and Clausura), each crowning one champion. [[C.D. Marathón]], as the team with the best record, qualified to the [[2019 CONCACAF Champions League]]. The first game of the season was played on 29 July between [[Club Deportivo Olimpia]] and new newcomers [[Lobos UPNFM]] which ended in a 1–0 victory for the home club.[http://www.lnphn.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Calendario-Oficial-Aprobado-Apertura-2017-2018.pdf LNPhn.com – Calendario de Juegos Primera Vuelta Campeonato de Apertura 2017-2018] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171026054020/http://www.lnphn.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Calendario-Oficial-Aprobado-Apertura-2017-2018.pdf |date=2017-10-26 }} – 14 July 2017 This game in fact corresponds to week 4, however, Olimpia requested a reschedule as they faced [[Liga Deportiva Alajuelense]] on that same week for the [[2017 CONCACAF League]]. On 18 August, la entire week 3 was cancelled due to a referee's strike, who requested for a salary increase which was rejected.[http://www.diariomas.hn/2017/08/18/arbitros-de-honduras-se-van-a-huelga/ DiarioMas.hn – Árbitros de Honduras se van a huelga] – 18 August 2017 On 2 September, [[C.D. Honduras Progreso]] played against Lobos UPNFM at [[Estadio Humberto Micheletti]], a game which was witnessed only by 56 spectators, one more over the current record implemented by [[Palestino F.C.]] v [[Pumas UNAH]] (55 in [[1997–98 Honduran Liga Nacional|1998]]). On 24 September, [[F.C. Motagua]] paid a visit to [[Platense F.C.]] at [[Estadio Excélsior]]; Motagua came with a long 21-game unbeaten run carried since last season; on the other hand, Platense were at the bottom of the league standings. Motagua scored 3 consecutive goals in the first 60 minutes of play to obtain a comfortable lead; however, in the last 20+ minutes of the match, Platense scored 4 goals to give the ''Selacios'' the most unlikely win of the season so far.{{cite web|title=¡Ta-ta! ¡Ta-ta!!!! Platense le remonta a un Motagua superior pero demasiado confiado|url=http://www.elheraldo.hn/deportes/1111068-466/ta-ta-ta-ta-platense-le-remonta-a-un-motagua-superior-pero-demasiado-confiado|website=El Heraldo|publisher=[[La Prensa (Honduras)|El Heraldo]]|access-date=24 September 2017}} On 19 November, [[C.D. Marathón]] defeated Olimpia 0–1 and clinched the first position in the regular standings for their fifth time in history.{{cite web|title=Marathon a semifinales al vencer a Olimpia en Honduras|url=http://ecodiario.eleconomista.es/internacional/noticias/8755527/11/17/Marathon-a-semifinales-al-vencer-a-Olimpia-en-Honduras.html|website=EcoDiario.es|publisher=[[El Economista (Spain)|El Economista]]|access-date=20 November 2017}} Three of the four playoff matches were rescheduled due to the [[Honduran general election, 2017|2017 Honduran political crisis]]. During the 1st leg of the semifinal between [[Real C.D. España]] and [[C.D. Marathón]], referee [[Armando Castro (referee)|Armando Castro]] gave Real España a non-existing penalty. Furious fans from the opposite side invaded the pitch and started throwing rocks to policemen and referees. Police answered with tear gas bombs and the authorities decided to suspend the match. The other semifinal between Olimpia and Motagua was also suspended due to lack of security guarantees. On 14 December, the League informed that without safety measures, they will not scheduled any other games until further notice.{{cite web|title=Clásico capitalino suspendido porque no hay garantías de seguridad|url=http://www.elpais.hn/2017/12/14/clasico-capitalino-suspendido-porque-no-hay-garantias-de-seguridad/|website=ElPaís.hn|publisher=[[La Tribuna (Honduras)|El País]]|access-date=14 December 2017}} On 18 December, due to the pressing situation, the League decided to play the rest of the tournament in closed doors, except for the final series. España]] player [[Javier Arnaldo Portillo|Javier Portillo]] sued the club due to a non-paid contract expiring in 2018. Portillo was sacked in October 2016 for unsporting conduct and passed over the agreement.[http://www.laprensa.hn/deportes/1007251-410/javier-portillo-queda-fuera-del-real-espa%C3%B1a LaPrensa.hn – Javier Portillo queda fuera del Real España] – 11 October 2017 The National Football Arbitration Court (''TNAF'') determined that the club must comply with the contract and pay Portillo the sum of [[Honduran lempira|L.]]1,050,000.00 before the start of the Apertura tournament.[http://www.diez.hn/liganacionaldehonduras/1095768-498/deuda_real_espa%C3%B1a-honduras_javier_portillo Diez.hn – Real España pagará deuda de más de un millón de lempiras a Javier Portillo] – 4 August 2017 On 5 August 2017, Real España played their first game of the season defeating [[Platense F.C.]] at [[Estadio Francisco Morazán]]. A few hours prior, the club had issued a non-negotiable check payable to ''TNAF'' and not to Portillo as the verdict demanded. As a result, and according to the league's disciplinary codes,[http://www.lnphn.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/01/Codigo-de-Disciplina.pdf LNPhn.com – CODIGO DISCIPLINARIO DE LA FEDERACION NACIONAL AUTONOMA DE FUTBOL] – July 2011 these breaches are penalized with the deduction of points until the debt is condoned, or even relegation to a lower tier. On 10 August 2017, [[Fuad Abufele]], president of Real España, threatened to withdraw from the league if any points are deducted.[http://tiempo.hn/real-espana-amenaza-la-liga-nacional/ Tiempo.hn – El Real España amenaza a la Liga Nacional si les quitan puntos] – 10 August 2017 A week later, Real España did finally issue the check payable to Portillo and the Appeal Commission decided not to deduct any points from Real España, thus contradicting their own regulations.[http://www.elpais.hn/2017/08/14/real-espana-solventa-tiempo-forma-deuda-javier-portillo/ ElPaís.hn – Real España solventa en tiempo y forma deuda con Javier Portillo] – 14 August 2017 Real España, however, is willing to take the case further to [[FIFA]].[http://www.laprensa.hn/deportes/1097704-410/fuad-abufele-a-javier-portillo-le-aconsejo-que-no-que-se-coma-ese-dinero-real-espa%C3%B1a LaPrensa.hn – Fuad Abufele a Javier Portillo: "Le aconsejo que no se coma ese dinero"] – 10 August 2017 * Due to a [[Referee (association football)|referee's]] strike who were demanding an increase in their salary, the entire week 3 in the ''Apertura'' tournament was suspended and had to be rescheduled.[http://radioamericahn.net/suspendida-jornada-primera-division-honduras-huelga-arbitros/ RadioAmericaHN.net – Suspendida jornada de primera división en Honduras por huelga de árbitros] – 20 August 2017 The tournament was resumed on week 4 and due to the tight schedule, the pending games were played during a [[FIFA International Match Calendar]]. * On weeks 7 and 12, [[C.D. Marathón]]'s defender [[Caue Fernandes]] injured [[Carlo Costly]] against [[Club Deportivo Olimpia]] and [[Eddie Hernández]] against [[F.C. Motagua]] respectively. Both injuries included serious fractures which had left both players out of competition for several weeks and consequently missing important [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONCACAF)|World Cup qualifying]] matches. In both occasions, Costly strongly criticized Fernandes for his actions calling him a #pig on his [[Twitter]] account.{{cite web|title=Carlo Costly arremete contra Caue Fernandes, tras lesionar a Eddie Hernández|url=http://www.elheraldo.hn/deportes/1118974-466/carlo-costly-arremete-contra-caue-fernandes-tras-lesionar-a-eddie-hern%C3%A1ndez|website=ElHeraldo.hn|publisher=[[La Prensa (Honduras)|El Heraldo]]|access-date=22 October 2017}} * [[Real C.D. Motagua]]'s foremen, due to his inconsistency when interpreting and enforcing the law. Right before the semifinals, the entity penalized [[Club Deportivo Olimpia]]'s midfielder [[Alexander López]] for one game only due to his violent conduct and a straight red card in a playoff game against [[Lobos UPNFM]]. López complied and was eligible to play against Motagua in the semifinals. However, the controversy arose when back in November UPNFM's midfielder [[Mayron Flores]] was given two games of suspension for exactly the same actions during a regular season match, consequently missing action against Olimpia in the playoffs. España]] and [[C.D. Marathón]] were playing for the first leg of the ''Apertura'' semifinals. In the 71st minute, the referee [[Armando Castro (referee)|Armando Castro]] called a non-existing penalty for Real España. Due to the controversial decision the Marathón's [[barra brava]] invaded the pitch and started trowing rocks at the referees and policemen. Real España's fans followed and tried to confront their rival's counterpart creating a chaos which ended up in the release of tear gas bombs. The game was suspended and was finally resumed eight days later on 21 December. The final 19 minutes of play were restarted with the penalty called one week prior in what was known as the longest match ever played in Honduras. * Prior the beginning of the ''Clausura'' tournament, five clubs ([[C.D. Vida]]) which represents 50% of the league, declared themselves financially inoperative and unwilling to start the competition unless the league or the government provides them with at least [[Honduran lempira|L.]]4,000,000 to each team to help them heal some debts. Coach [[Salomón Nazar]] complained that the dressing rooms didn't have water for his players to take showers after the match, having to do so outdoors with buckets.{{cite web|title=¡Penoso! Motagua]]'s forward [[Román Castillo]] scored his 73rd goal with his club. Some media, statistic experts and historians claim that former player [[Ángel Obando]] scored 77 goals with Motagua between 1974 and 1986 and he has been the club's top-goalscorer for over 40 years. However, Motagua published on their social accounts their own list where Obando appears at the top of the list but with 73 goals only. If the club's numbers are correct, Castillo was now sharing the record along with Obando. The league was consulted by a local newspaper about the controversy to clarify this and to have an official version.
